A video of the incident circulating on social media showed the minister, a trained medical doctor, kneeling beside the woman and attending to her with the assistance of other people before paramedics arrived. She was also seen giving instructions on how the woman should be positioned while efforts were made to assist her. The identity of the woman and her condition after the incident have not been made public. Agyeman-Rawlings’ intervention has attracted praise on social media, with many commending her for putting her medical training to use during the emergency. Some users described her response as an example of leadership and compassion, while others used the incident to highlight the importance of learning basic first aid and CPR. The minister, who is the daughter of Ghana’s late former President Jerry John Rawlings, trained as a medical doctor at the Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland before entering politics. She was sworn in as Ghana’s Minister for Environment, Science and Technology in August 2026. Her intervention at the climate conference has also prompted conversations online about her leadership potential, with some social media users asking whether she could become a future presidential contender.
